sentences.text: Eostrix is an extinct genus of primitive owls belonging to the family Protostrigidae.
The smaller species, E. martinellii, was roughly the size of a modern long-eared owl.
This bird is distinguished from living owls by unique grooves on its tarsometatarsus, including a groove for digit 2, a deep posterior groove for digit 3, and a rounded trochlea for digit 4.
The genus Eostrix was established by Pierce Brodkorb in 1971 to reclassify the species formerly known as Protostrix mimica.
The species E. mimica was described by Alexander Wetmore in 1938 based on hindlimb elements found in Eocene strata in Wyoming.
The species E. martinellii was described in 1972 from a left tarsometatarsus found by Jorge Martinelli in 1970 in Fremont County, Wyoming, within the Lysite member of the Wind River Formation.
The species E. vincenti was described by Colin Harrison in 1980 from early Eocene London Clay in England.
The species E. tsaganica was described in 2011 by Evgeny Kurochkin and Gareth J. Dyke from fossils found in Mongolia.
Gerald Mayr described the species E. gulottai in 2016 from the early Eocene Nanjemoy Formation in Virginia.
Eostrix fossils date from the early Eocene and have been found in the United States, Europe, and Mongolia.
Eostrix lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
Some scholars debate whether E. vincenti belongs in the genus Eostrix or resembles the genus Necrobyas more closely.
